correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening, southern bend and northeastward continuation
correspondence.finding: The opening and southern/eastward bend lie in the mapped Inland Ice south and southwest of Vildtland. The following northeastward approach remains in the broad continental-ice setting. The national map covers the whole selected area south of the detailed sheet's 81°N edge.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The map's surface contours, ice-thickness bands and bedrock contours are not natural-river traces or proof of subglacial drainage.

correspondence.component_scope: Long northward approach toward southern Vildtland
correspondence.finding: The northward connector continues through Inland Ice and enters the southern Vildtland margin setting. National and detailed map coverage overlap before the major eastward turn. The detailed sheet distinguishes the broad ice area from exposed terrain and superficial-deposit margins.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: No named river or natural source point is established. No unseen segment is inferred solely from the model's connectivity.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward connector along the southern Vildtland margin
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward and southeastward steps occupy the southern Vildtland ice/land-margin corridor, with mapped superficial deposits and scattered exposed areas, before approaching the western side of Academy Gletscher. The original sheet covers the complete connector.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: This describes the corridor setting, not an exact surveyed channel, uniform surface cover at every model vertex or a continuous natural-river name. No selected through-lake passage or separately named tributary is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward lower approach and actual terminal corridor
correspondence.finding: The lower route turns north in the Academy Gletscher setting, between Vildtland to the west and Academy Land to the east, and ends in its inner-Independence-Fjord glacier/front corridor. The original detailed map distinguishes this from Marie Sophie Gletscher farther north and the Hagen Bræ/Hagen Fjord corridor farther east.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized terminal-corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Retained model terminal class sea is metadata. Historical mapped glacier/fjord geography does not establish a current river mouth, exact contemporary front position, flow direction or glacier name as a river hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward storage and initial Tlaxcala corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected initial southward approach occupies the southeastern Tlaxco/Lázaro Cárdenas storage setting, then curves east and north into the Emiliano Zapata Apulco corridor. The state sheet and adjoining municipal maps show the small Lázaro Cárdenas waterbody, its downstream channel setting, El Gachupin and Tenexac reach labels and the northward exit. The southern Tenexac reservoir is a separately mapped feeder/storage setting and is not claimed as a selected crossing. The first feeder and exact transitions among these local labels remain unnamed in this finding; geographic correspondence does not require one name for them.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Emiliano Zapata–Ixtacamaxtitlán–Zautla upper Apulco
correspondence.finding: The route runs northeast from the western Emiliano Zapata channel into Puebla, meets the independently mapped Los Lobos western approach, turns east through the Ixtacamaxtitlán canyon and bends northeast/north by Las Barrancas, Tlamanca and Santiago Zautla. Direct Apulco labels and the mapped course support this reach identity. The western Los Lobos branch is not substituted for the selected southern approach.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Apulco and Laguna la Soledad
correspondence.finding: North of Santiago Zautla the selected course follows the valley west of Cinco de Mayo and Zacapoaxtla, turns northeast by Huahuaxtla, then east south of Cuetzalan via the San Juan Tahitic–Calatepec–Tepetzintla corridor. Original state cartography shows entry into Laguna la Soledad, its eastward outlet and the subsequent northward river corridor east of Cuetzalan. The waterbody passage is retained separately rather than called Tecolutla throughout. The mapped hydroelectric setting is context only; current operations and diversion proportions were not established.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.mapped_component_name: Apulco; Laguna la Soledad is a separate waterbody identity

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Apulco approach and lateral junctions
correspondence.finding: Below the Soledad setting the route turns north and northwest through the lower valley west of Ayotoxco de Guerrero and Tenampulco, passing the San Antonio Rayón/Buena Vista area toward the Espinal junction. Municipal cartography distinguishes the southern Apulco approach from Zempoala and the western Tecacan/El Zapote channels. The selected mainstem reaches the material western-branch junction just before the downstream Tecolutla corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Short selected western tributary
correspondence.finding: The entire short western selected component follows the lower Necaxa approach through southern Espinal municipality, eastward then southeastward to meet the selected Apulco approach. The original Espinal relief map directly labels Necaxa on that western corridor and Tecolutla downstream. This finding identifies only the retained short component, not an unselected full Necaxa system, and does not rename it Tecolutla.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Tecolutla river and coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: From the Apulco–Necaxa junction the selected river turns east and northeast by Espinal, continues north through the Paso de Valencia–San Gotardo–Agua Dulce corridor, then meanders east past the Carrillo Puerto/Lomas de Arena setting to Gutiérrez Zamora and Tecolutla. The original state map and municipal relief map show the actual Gulf of Mexico outlet at Barra de Tecolutla. The neighboring Estero Lagartos and Estero La Victoria are not substituted for this outlet. No exact modeled extension, bank position or contemporary mouth-bar state is asserted.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Davidson Mountains headward branch
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is an unlabeled mountain stream northwest of the later Firth junction. The original USGSTopo view shows its entire initial southeastward valley, joining minor branches, the eastward valley continuation and the further southeastward descent. The selection remains in the same mapped channel corridor through those changes of direction. NLUIS117B corroborates the mountain-valley setting and the lower part of this branch.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The opening branch has no securely read hydronym in these originals. It is not assigned the names of nearby Mancha Creek or of the separate southern Firth headwater. No exact natural source or exhaustive minor-branch inventory is established.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern bend and joining with the labeled Firth
correspondence.finding: At the broad southern bend, the selected northwestern valley joins a separate stream arriving from the south that USGSTopo labels Firth River. The joined braided corridor turns east and northeast, where repeated Firth River labels occur in USGSTopo and NLUIS117B. The separate southern headwater is contextual and is not the selected opening.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The junction and valley sequence are read at normal corridor scale; the exact naming-transition vertex and individual active braids are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Alaska–Yukon border and upper Canadian valley
correspondence.finding: The joined river continues northeast through the broad valley to the international boundary. Mancha Creek is shown as a separate western/northwestern branch entering the Firth near the border setting. The selected river crosses into Yukon and continues northeast along the labeled Firth corridor in the British Mountains. Side channels and wet alluvial flats are drawn, rather than a selected lake or reservoir.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Mancha Creek, its separate upstream tributaries and the unselected southern Firth source valley are not included as alternative scalar names for the selected feature.

correspondence.component_scope: British Mountains northward course and Joe Creek junction
correspondence.finding: NLUIS117B follows the Firth northeast and then north, including the eastern Muskeg Creek joining system. The northward river crosses the sheet boundary into NLUIS117C, makes a westward bend and meets the separately labeled Joe Creek from the southwest/west. It then turns northeast again. Both sides of the sheet seam and the full joining sequence are visible in the originals.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Muskeg Creek and Joe Creek remain distinct tributaries. An administrative or wildlife overlay is not treated as hydrography. The cartographic seam is covered without requiring an exact model vertex match.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle northeastward corridor and Sheep Creek setting
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues northeast down the labeled Firth valley. Sheep Creek, including its separate Porcupine Creek branch, joins from the northwest in NLUIS117C. The main river then continues east toward the Herschel Island sheet. The adjoining NLUIS117D original shows the same eastward entry and the subsequent northeastward and northward river course.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The neighboring Malcolm River is separately mapped and is not a Firth alias or selected tributary. Porcupine Creek is contextual within the Sheep Creek branch; its whole course is not part of the selected mainstem.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower gorge, foothills and coastal-plain transition
correspondence.finding: NLUIS117D follows the complete selected lower river from the mountain gorge, with mapped rapids/falls, into the foothill and coastal plain. Loney Creek is shown joining from the west. The river becomes a broad, divided channel corridor on the plain. Its own marginal R4 description independently describes the Firth gorge between the Sheep Creek setting and the coastal plain.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The historic map establishes the corridor and historical named context, not current whitewater conditions, a particular active braid or a present-day bank. No inland lake or reservoir passage is depicted along the selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual coastal delta and receiving-water setting
correspondence.finding: The selected northward river reaches the broad delta and coastal-water margin south of Nunaluk Spit and southwest of Herschel Island. Original NLUIS117D pixels show the river continuing into its divided delta, the barrier-spit coast, nearby Workboat Passage, Herschel Island and the Beaufort Sea setting. The separate Malcolm River delta lies to the west. This is direct terminal-context reading, not a sea assignment from basin association alone.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: No exact modern mouth point, shoreline, distributary choice or bank fit is claimed. The selected generalized terminal extension is read within the actual delta/coastal setting. Workboat Passage, Nunaluk Spit and Herschel Island are distinct geographic context, not river aliases; no separately verified lagoon name is assigned.
correspondence.mapped_component_name: Firth River / Beaufort Sea coastal waters

correspondence.component_scope: western headward setting and initial feeder
correspondence.finding: Wardle’s map shows the lake-and-stream country beside the Quebec–Labrador divide southeast of the Lac Machault area. The selected headward leg lies in that small-waterbody setting, turns northwest and then northeast into the eastward chain. The individual selected feeder and pond names are not established. Anderson’s whole-system figure independently depicts this western branched headwater setting.
correspondence.correspondence: observed at ordinary generalized headwater scale
correspondence.limits: The regional map is used for component/corridor correspondence, not a claim of precise source-pond identity, legal provincial-boundary placement or exact small-channel vertices.

correspondence.component_scope: western lake and steady chain into the middle valley
correspondence.finding: Wardle’s northern map sector follows the connected, irregular eastward lake/stream chain south of Mistastin Lake into the broader middle valley. The chain continues into the overlapping western edge of Hill’s Notakwanon area sheet. Anderson’s upper river network and prose describe a long upstream series of steadies. No name is assigned to the individual lake passages.
correspondence.correspondence: observed

correspondence.component_scope: north-turning middle reach and long eastward valley
correspondence.finding: Hill’s 1:100,000 map directly shows the marked Notakwanon River valley turning north through the middle of its map, then bending east through the broad lower-relief corridor. These successive turns correspond to the selected middle reach. Side valleys and north- and south-side tributary/lake systems are separately drawn and are not renamed as the selected mainstem.
correspondence.correspondence: observed

correspondence.component_scope: eastern bend and lower river approaching the coast
correspondence.finding: The overlapping Hill and Wardle maps distinguish the main valley from the southern Sango drainage. Wardle’s northern margin continues the selected northeastward bend and east-running lower valley toward the coastal sector, while Anderson Figure107 depicts the lower main river separately from incoming branches and carries it onward to Merrifield Bay.
correspondence.correspondence: observed at corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: short terminal continuation and receiving-water setting
correspondence.finding: Anderson’s original Figure107 traces the lower main river into the explicitly labelled Merrifield Bay. The accompanying account and Table376 identify the same river mouth setting. Wardle’s regional original supplies the surrounding named Merrifield Bay, Sango Bay and Labrador Sea geography. The short final selected fragment is a continuation of this terminal river setting, not a separately established tributary hydronym.
correspondence.correspondence: observed at ordinary river-to-bay scale
correspondence.limits: Wardle’s neatline ends at the northern coastal margin; Anderson supplies the actual river-to-bay connection. Exact modern shoreline, tidal limits and the selected render endpoint are not validated.

correspondence.component_scope: material lake and tributary scope
correspondence.finding: The original maps show an upper chain of small lakes/steadies, an intervening river valley and tributary junctions, then the lower river ending in a coastal bay. No reservoir or passage through the separate northern Mistastin Lake is invoked to connect the selected route. All unestablished local feeder, tributary and lake names remain null.
correspondence.correspondence: observed
